--- DRAFT FOR MEDHEALTH SECURITY ---
PHI boundary summary (Redwood Inference):
- We treat any data that contains personally identifiable health information as PHI. Redwood Hosted API is multitenant and may use shared serving infrastructure and ephemeral KV caches; it is not eligible for PHI workloads.
- Redwood Dedicated provides customer-dedicated GPU pools and logical isolation; with a signed BAA and agreed configuration, Dedicated can be used for PHI processing (data-in-memory; we do not persist raw prompt/response tokens unless configured for logging).
- Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) is the recommended option for highest isolation: customer manages networking and can plug in customer KMS/HSM for key separation.

Controls / notes:
- Logging & metrics: by default we collect aggregated telemetry for performance SLOs. For PHI workloads we offer opt-out or filtered logs; specific retention policies are contractable.
- KV caches: persistent KV caches are only used in Dedicated/Private and can be configured not to persist to disk; Hosted uses ephemeral caches on shared instances.
- Encryption: in transit TLS 1.2+ and at-rest encryption for any persisted artifacts. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations.
- SOC 2: Redwood is in active SOC 2 Type II audit window; expected completion Q2 2026. We can share the current SOC 2 interim report under NDA.

Next steps (for MedHealth):
1) Marissa: send this draft to MedHealth security with the BAA primer and note that Dedicated/Private are the eligible deployment modes.
2) Legal: once we receive the completed questionnaire, route to legal for BAA discussion.

--- end draft ---
